In [[mathematics]], two '''Prüfer theorems''', named after [[Heinz Prüfer]], describe the structure of certain [[infinite group|infinite]] [[abelian group]]s. They have been generalized by L. Ya. Kulikov.

== Statement ==

Let ''A'' be an abelian group. If ''A'' is [[finitely generated abelian group|finitely generated]] then by the [[fundamental theorem of finitely generated abelian groups]], ''A'' is decomposable into a [[direct sum]] of [[cyclic group|cyclic]] [[subgroup]]s, which leads to the classification of finitely generated abelian groups [[up to]] [[group isomorphism|isomorphism]]. The structure of general infinite abelian groups can be considerably more complicated and the conclusion needs not to hold, but Prüfer [[mathematical proof|proved]] that it remains true for [[periodic group]]s in two special cases.

The '''first Prüfer theorem''' states that an abelian group of bounded [[exponent (group theory)|exponent]] is isomorphic to a direct sum of cyclic groups. The '''second Prüfer theorem''' states that a [[countable set|countable]] abelian ''p''-group whose non-trivial elements have finite [[height (abelian group)|''p''-height]] is isomorphic to a direct sum of cyclic groups. Examples show that the assumption that the group be countable cannot be removed.

The two Prüfer theorems follow from a general criterion of decomposability of an abelian group into a direct sum of cyclic subgroups due to L. Ya. Kulikov:
<blockquote>
An abelian [[p-group|''p''-group]] ''A'' is isomorphic to a direct sum of cyclic groups if and only if it is a [[union (set theory)|union]] of a sequence {''A''<sub>''i''</sub>} of subgroups with the property that the heights of all elements of ''A''<sub>''i''</sub> are bounded by a constant (possibly depending on ''i'').
</blockquote>
